questions.text: A hospital quality department is embedded within individual clinical units rather than housed as a central department. Quality staff report directly to unit leaders and are integrated into daily unit operations. This BEST describes which organizational structure?
questions.explanation: Decentralized quality structures place quality expertise closer to frontline teams and local workflows. This increases responsiveness and unit-level ownership but may reduce enterprise-wide standardization.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the primary purpose of the peer review process in a healthcare organization?

options.a: Verifying physician credentials before granting hospital privileges
options.b: Retrospectively evaluating a clinician's clinical performance and identifying improvement opportunities
options.c: Assessing organizational readiness for accreditation surveys
options.d: Reviewing patient safety incident reports at the unit level

questions.explanation: Peer review is a retrospective process where qualified colleagues evaluate clinical decisions and outcomes to identify performance improvement opportunities. It is distinct from credentialing, which verifies qualifications before granting privileges.

questions.text: A steering committee is formed to guide the implementation of a new sepsis protocol across all inpatient units. Which of the following BEST describes the committee's primary governance function?

options.a: Oversee the organization's overall quality strategy and performance governance
options.b: Guide the specific improvement initiative and remove implementation barriers
options.c: Credential clinical staff involved in sepsis management
options.d: Review retrospective mortality data for root cause analysis

questions.explanation: Steering committees are formed to guide specific improvement initiatives and remove barriers to implementation. Quality councils, by contrast, oversee the broader organizational quality strategy.

questions.text: A quality professional is asked to help a clinical department reduce medication errors. Rather than auditing the department, the quality professional facilitates a team problem-solving session, analyzes process data, and helps design a workflow improvement. This role BEST reflects:

options.b: The quality department as an organizational partner and improvement facilitator

questions.explanation: The CPHQ framework positions quality professionals as facilitators, advisors, and improvement partners — not auditors or compliance enforcement agents. Technical expertise is deployed to support, not police, clinical teams.

questions.text: Which of the following quality organizational structures BEST supports both enterprise-wide standardization AND unit-level improvement accountability?
questions.explanation: Matrix and hybrid structures connect central quality oversight with departmental ownership and accountability — balancing the standardization benefits of centralization with the frontline responsiveness of decentralization.
